khai.tagline: Politics as process: how a persona gets an outcome out of a body that decides collectively, where the rule for deciding is itself in play -- across the three faces a contest can sit at (the open contest, the agenda, the settled premise), the seven levers that work on the situation rather than on anybody's mind (agenda-setting, dimension-splitting, scope-shifting, coalition-building, logrolling, stalling, the rule contest), and the five footings that make a lever bite (the veto point, the broker seat, the bloc, the mandate, the outsider) -- with the twist that the most complete victory produces the least visible activity (Dahl; Bachrach & Baratz; Lukes; Schattschneider; Riker).

card.wire: Attaches at Persona. The root (process_politics.md) declares politics as what a persona does where the outcome is not theirs to decide and the rule for deciding is itself something that can be moved. It is not persuasion and not bargaining: the characteristic political move changes the situation so that the existing preferences produce a different result, without anybody's mind having been altered. Arrow's impossibility is the reason the domain exists -- there is no neutral way to add preferences up, so the rule is always a party to the outcome and always worth contesting.
card.issue: Three altitudes, one core. The faces: where the contest actually sits -- the open contest, decided by who has the numbers on a question already on the table; the agenda, decided by what reaches the table at all; and the settled premise, where the question is not raised because nobody has been given a way to want it raised. The levers: seven moves that work on the situation rather than on anybody's mind -- agenda-setting, dimension-splitting, scope-shifting, coalition-building, logrolling, stalling, and the rule contest. The footings: five things a persona may hold that make a lever bite -- the veto point, the broker seat, the bloc, the mandate, and the outsider's stand, which is the absence of the other four and leaves only one lever available.
card.require: Two altitudes hold the engine. The law: declared once in the project's Instructions Knowledge chapter, linking the root, so the politics read runs wherever a body decides anything. The link: each persona links, under Projection, the face they are contesting at, the levers available to them, and the footing they hold.
card.enforce: Structure is checked; the read is judged. The kit verifies the law is declared and each persona links a real face, lever, and footing. Whether a persona's move is genuinely heresthetic rather than rhetorical, and whether a body's quiet is a settled premise or simple agreement, is semantic -- taught and reviewed, never failed by the suite.
card.setup: Declare the law in the Instructions Knowledge chapter, linking the root. Then, for each persona who wants something a body must decide, link the face the contest sits at, the levers their footing permits, and the footing itself. Give the body a rule and let the rule be contestable, since a body whose procedure is fixed and neutral has no politics in it. Keep the levers situational: a persona who wins by changing minds has run swaying and not this. And read a quiet body carefully, because quiet is the signature of the third face and also of ordinary agreement, and the engine does not tell them apart.
